gaps.sentence: I ___ dinner when the lights went out.
gaps.hint: the lights went out interrupted it
gaps.explanation: The lights going out interrupted an ongoing background action, so the past continuous is used: was cooking.

gaps.sentence: This month they ___ a new wing to the hospital, so some services are elsewhere.
gaps.hint: this month means a temporary current period
gaps.explanation: 'This month' describes a temporary situation around now, so the present continuous fits: are adding.

gaps.sentence: The bridge ___ to traffic every year for repainting in May.
gaps.explanation: A recurring scheduled event takes the present simple.

gaps.sentence: The play ___ when we reached the theatre, so we missed the first scene.
gaps.hint: it started before we reached it
gaps.explanation: The starting happened before the past moment of arriving, so the past perfect fits: had already started.

gaps.sentence: He ___ in the garden when the storm broke.
gaps.explanation: An action in progress interrupted by a short event — past continuous.

gaps.sentence: When I got home, I realised I ___ my keys at the office.
gaps.explanation: 'Had left' — the leaving happened before the realising.

gaps.sentence: The phone is ringing. Don't worry, I ___ it.
gaps.hint: a spontaneous decision at the moment
gaps.explanation: Decisions made at the moment of speaking use 'will': will answer.

gaps.sentence: The taxi ___ as soon as you come out of the terminal — look for a blue shirt.
gaps.hint: in progress at the future arrival moment
gaps.explanation: An action that will be in progress at a future moment takes the future continuous: will be waiting.
